question: Should existing GitHub-backed skills with over-40-character stored display names be grandfathered like hosted skills, or intentionally shortened on the next sync?
rationale: The PR chooses a compatibility-sensitive policy for stored catalog metadata, and source inspection shows current sync would rewrite existing GitHub-backed titles without maintainer-visible approval.

options.title: Grandfather GitHub-backed legacy names
options.body: Preserve unchanged existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names and only enforce the limit for new or renamed GitHub-backed entries.

options.title: Accept sync-time shortening
options.body: Treat GitHub-backed over-limit titles as intentionally migratable on next sync, but document that policy and add upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause display-name policy
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers choose both the public maximum length and legacy handling for hosted and GitHub-backed skills.

recommendation.title: Grandfather GitHub-backed legacy names
recommendation.body: Preserve unchanged existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names and only enforce the limit for new or renamed GitHub-backed entries.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen owns the strongest recent history on the GitHub-backed sync and shared publish paths affected by the policy decision.
